What comes up in Box Hill

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. What follows is how this work normally runs in the area, not a reading of any one block.

Clearing a rural holding for release

Sheds, fencing, concrete, vegetation and sometimes a dwelling, on land that is about to become an estate.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials assessed and removed first, then the structures and vegetation off by stream, and the block left clear for the civil works.
What does it
Large excavator with a grapple and a mulcher where the volume suits it.

Bulk earthworks to the civil design

Moving and placing material to bring the land to the levels the design calls for.

How it is handled
Cut and fill balanced across the site where it can be, with imported material placed and compacted in layers rather than tipped and spread.
What does it
Large excavators, roller, truck and dogs in both directions.

Slabs, footings and hardstand

What is left in the ground once the building is gone, and whether it comes out depends entirely on what is going on top of it.

How it is handled
Broken out with a hammer where it is coming out, or left and built over where the new design allows it. Worth settling with the builder before the quote rather than after.
What does it
Excavator with a hydraulic hammer, and a screening or grading bucket to finish the level.

Box Hill

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Growth land under subdivision Which makes bulk earthworks, fill and site preparation the dominant work rather than knockdowns.
  • Rural holdings being released Still carrying sheds, dams, fencing, concrete and the occasional house.
  • Levels set by the civil design And the job is quoted to a nominated platform level and tolerance.
  • Clay rich soils Which behave very differently wet and dry, and are classified differently from sand when they leave.

Box Hill sites are generally open with room for large plant and good truck access on the main roads, though the internal estate roads change week to week while an estate is being built out. Sequencing against the civil programme matters more here than plant size.

Box Hill questions

What people ask before we start

Do you do bulk earthworks on estate land?
Yes. Bulk excavation, site cut and levelling, and fill supply and placement are the main work in the growth areas, and the same contract covers the clearing that comes before it.
What about an old dam or farm structure on the block?
It is scoped like anything else. Dams are drained, dried and filled with suitable material compacted in layers, and farm structures are assessed for hazardous materials before they come down.
There are large trees on the block. How does that work?
Tree removal depends on approval rather than on plant, and in this area it is routinely the longest item on a clearing programme. Retained trees need their root zones kept clear of plant and stockpiles, which frequently decides where the machine goes.
How many contractors am I dealing with if there is asbestos on site?
One. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, licensed asbestos removalists carry out the removal, and an independent licensed assessor does the air monitoring and clearance. Sequencing the three of them is our job, not yours.
